Evaluation metrics

Source: R/graph-evaluation.R
metrics.Rd

Task metrics computed on plain R vectors, so they can be used with any model. Classification metrics take the true class and the predicted class; ranking metrics take scores (higher means more likely positive).

Usage

metric_accuracy(truth, estimate)

metric_balanced_accuracy(truth, estimate)

metric_precision(truth, estimate, average = "macro", positive = NULL)

metric_recall(truth, estimate, average = "macro", positive = NULL)

metric_f1(truth, estimate, average = "macro", positive = NULL)

metric_roc_auc(truth, score)

metric_average_precision(truth, score)

metric_ece(truth, prob, bins = 10L)

metric_brier(truth, prob)

metric_mse(truth, estimate)

metric_rmse(truth, estimate)

metric_mae(truth, estimate)

metric_r2(truth, estimate)

metric_hits_at_k(pos, neg, k = 10L)

metric_mrr(pos, neg)

metric_nmi(truth, cluster)

metric_ari(truth, cluster)

Arguments

truth

True values: factor or integer classes, 0/1 or logical for binary ranking metrics, numeric for regression.

estimate

Predicted class or value.

average

"macro" or "micro" averaging over classes, or "binary" for the class named by positive.

positive

Positive class for binary averaging.

score

Predicted score or probability of the positive class (or a probability matrix with one column per class for metric_roc_auc() and metric_ece()).

prob

Probability matrix (one column per class) or vector of positive class probabilities.

bins

Number of equal width bins.

pos

Scores of positive pairs.

neg

Scores of negative pairs: a vector shared by all positives, or a matrix with one row per positive.

k

Cut-off.

cluster

Cluster assignment.

Value

A numeric scalar.

Details

  • metric_roc_auc(): area under the ROC curve via the Mann-Whitney statistic, with ties counted one half. For a probability matrix and factor truth with more than two levels it returns the macro average of one-vs-rest AUCs.

  • metric_average_precision(): \(\sum_n (R_n - R_{n-1}) P_n\) over distinct score thresholds (the definition used by scikit-learn), not the trapezoidal area under the precision-recall curve.

  • metric_ece(): expected calibration error with equal width bins on the top predicted probability.

  • metric_hits_at_k(), metric_mrr(): link ranking metrics. With a vector of shared negatives, Hits@K is the fraction of positives scored above the K-th highest negative (the OGB ogbl-collab convention). With a matrix of per positive negatives (one row per positive), the rank of each positive among its own negatives is used, ties counted one half.

Examples

truth <- factor(c("a", "b", "a", "b"))
est <- factor(c("a", "b", "b", "b"))
metric_accuracy(truth, est)
#> [1] 0.75
metric_f1(truth, est)
#> [1] 0.7333333
metric_roc_auc(c(1, 0, 1, 0), c(0.9, 0.2, 0.4, 0.5))
#> [1] 0.75
metric_hits_at_k(c(0.9, 0.3), c(0.5, 0.4, 0.1), k = 1)
#> [1] 0.5
